hero.headline: Linear, stop gating landing page iteration behind a merge request.

valueProps.title: Marketer-owned page iteration
valueProps.body: Linear's engineers move fast. Prismic's Visual Builder gives your marketing team the same velocity — draft, preview, and publish landing pages independently, without filing a ticket or waiting on a deploy.

valueProps.title: ABM pages that match your ICP precision
valueProps.body: Linear sells to high-performance software teams across verticals. Prismic's ABM Agent detects inbound company IP and serves a personalised page variant in real time — no bespoke dev work per account.

valueProps.title: Structured content that scales with 25,000 teams
valueProps.body: Slice Machine enforces a typed content model so every new page variant, locale, or campaign inherits Linear's design system — consistent at scale, without design review bottlenecks.

trustBar.headline: Trusted by product-led teams building at scale

fitSection.headline: Built for teams already running a PLG motion

closingCta.headline: See a Linear-branded ABM page generate live.
closingCta.body: No redesign, no migration. We connect to your existing front-end and show you a working personalised page within one session. Your engineers stay in their sprint.

growthBrief.opportunityTitle: Linear has no ABM content layer — 25K teams and a $1.25B valuation with zero personalised landing page infrastructure

rationaleBlocks.title: The gap
bullets: Linear's growth is **purely PLG and word-of-mouth** — no visible ABM instrumentation, no personalised landing pages, no account-specific conversion layer.
The marketing site uses a **custom-coded, engineer-maintained** front-end; every copy or layout change requires a pull request and deploy cycle.
Competitors like Asana, Clickup, and Atlassian **run aggressive paid and ABM programs** targeting Linear's ICP — Linear has no personalised response surface.
**HubSpot** is confirmed in the stack but there is no observable CMS or structured content layer feeding personalised web experiences from it.

rationaleBlocks.title: The math
bullets: Linear targets software teams at companies with 10–500 engineers — a segment where **ABM conversion lifts of 20–40%** on inbound traffic are well-documented.
Rough estimate: if **5% of monthly inbound visits** (conservative for a $100M ARR PLG product) convert at even a marginal uplift from personalised pages, incremental ARR is material.
Prismic Enterprise ACV sits in the **€60K–€180K range** for teams at this scale and content volume; mid-point assumption used for opportunity figure.
Opportunity sized at **€120K/month** in incremental pipeline value Linear could attribute to ABM-assisted conversions — rough, based on observed traffic tier and deal size band.

rationaleBlocks.title: What Prismic Agents ship
bullets: **ABM Agent** — reverse-IP detection triggers a company-specific hero, logo, and proof point without a new deploy; targets named accounts from Linear's outbound list.
**SEO Agent** — generates and maintains programmatic comparison pages (e.g. 'Linear vs Jira for fintech teams') capturing high-intent switcher queries Linear currently misses.
**Localization Agent** — Linear's Tokyo launch is live in the product UI; the marketing site has no localised landing pages for JP, DE, or FR markets, leaving enterprise pipeline on the table.
**Paid Ads Agent** — syncs page variants to paid campaigns, removing the eng bottleneck on post-click landing page iteration for any future paid investment.

rationaleBlocks.title: Why now
bullets: Linear closed an **$82M Series C in June 2025** — growth mode is on, headcount growing, marketing investment expected to scale.
Atlassian and Clickup are **increasing paid spend** against Linear's ICP; without a personalised content layer, Linear's inbound conversion rate is structurally capped.
Linear's **Tokyo expansion** signals intent to localise — Prismic Localization Agent is the fastest path from product locale to full marketing-site localisation.
The engineering team is small (~178 people total); **removing marketing's dependency on eng** for web content is an immediate operational win.

growthBrief.quickWin: **Build** one Prismic-powered ABM page targeting a named enterprise account segment (e.g. fintech companies 200–500 engineers) and **measure** demo-request conversion rate against the current generic homepage CTA over a two-week window. Use Linear's existing HubSpot data to seed the account list. Expected signal: 15–30% lift in demo requests from that segment within the test period.
